chunks: From him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Dawud ibn Suleyman Al-Hammaar, from Saeed ibn Yasar who said:

We sought permission to enter upon Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him); I, and Al-Harith ibn Al-Mughira Al-Nasry, and Mansour Al-Sayaqal. So we agreed to meet at the house of Tahir, his slave. So we prayed Al-Asr, then we went to him. We found him leaning on a bed near the ground, so we sat around him. Then he sat upright, then extended his legs until he placed his feet on the ground.
Then he said: 'Praise is to Allah, Who caused the people to go right and left: a Murji'ite sect, a Khawarij sect, a Qadariyya sect, and you have been named the Turabiyya.'

Then he said to the one on his right: 'By Allah, it is not except Allah, Alone, with no partner, and His Messenger, and the Progeny of His Messenger (peace be upon him and his family), and their Shias, may Allah honor their faces.'

And whoever was not upon that, was not upon anything. By Allah, Ali was the most worthy of the people to the people after the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family). He said it three times.

key_terms.آلُ رَسُولِهِ: The Progeny of the Messenger (Ahl al-Bayt)
key_terms.أَوْلَى النَّاسِ بِالنَّاسِ: The most worthy of the people to the people (leadership/authority)
key_terms.التُّرَابِيَّةَ: Turabiyyah (a sect named after the Prophet's title 'Tranquility of the Earth')

ai.seo_question: What are the four sects mentioned by Imam Al-Sadiq and who is considered the most worthy leader after the Prophet?
ai.summary: Imam Al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) uses this occasion to delineate the theological landscape of his era, critiquing the Murji'ah, Khawarij, Qadariyyah, and Turabiyyah sects while affirming the centrality of the Ahl al-Bayt. He concludes by emphatically declaring Imam Ali’s (peace be upon him) right to leadership (Wilayah) as the most rightful among people after the Prophet, a core Shia doctrine. This narration serves as a concise summary of early Shia identity and theological distinctiveness against contemporary sects.
